The problem encompasses labour allocation, configuration optimisation, and production planning. The objective is to minimise the total cost, including reconfiguration, exploitation, energy consumption, inventory, and stockout costs. A two-stage stochastic programming model is introduced, where the first stage includes labour allocation, configuration optimisation, and planned production quantity decisions in all periods, while the second stage captures scenario-dependent recourse decisions through inventory and stockouts. To solve the model, we develop a column generation algorithm (CG) and a CG-GAT algorithm that integrates CG with a multi-head Graph Attention Network. We conduct numerical experiments to compare the performance of state-of-the-art algorithm and the proposed algorithms. Numerical results show that CG-GAT outperforms the others. This work further provides managerial insights.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2695237.a: Selective maintenance problems are intensively investigated by both scholars and practitioners. Nonetheless, existing research on such problems usually overlooks the comprehensive consideration of diverse decision criteria and uncertain maintenance environments in terms of stochastic mission and break durations. This work proposes a stochastic multi-objective selective maintenance problem that considers stochastic mission and break durations and puts forward the corresponding optimisation method. First, a stochastic multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear chance-constrained programming model is constructed to maximise mission reliability and minimise maintenance cost under maintenance time constraints. Second, a learning-driven multi-objective artificial bee colony algorithm is tailored to tackle the proposed model. In the designed approach, a Q-learning method in the employed bee phase and an iterative local search method in the onlooker phase are deployed to enhance the exploration and exploitation abilities. Finally, through conducting comparison experiments between the customised method and five popular methods on several real-world cases, the experimental results confirm its feasibility and superiority in addressing the problem of interest.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2695238.a: As the demand for personalised customisation increases, manufacturing enterprises are continually enhancing their capabilities to meet diverse market requirements. This paper investigates a two-stage assembly flowshop scheduling problem, focusing on minimising total tardiness while accounting for resource flexibility and dynamic product arrivals using multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL). To explore the operational benefits of resource flexibility in scheduling environments, a skill matrix is introduced to assess the flexibility level of the processing machines. The problem is modelled as a Markov decision process (MDP), and a Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimisation algorithm with an Epsilon-greedy approach (E-MAPPO) is proposed for product sequencing and processing machine allocation. Experimental results show that, across different numbers of arrival products and flexibility levels, the scheduling agent trained with the E-MAPPO effectively learns to apply suitable dispatching rules. Notably, the algorithm outperforms 18 composite dispatching rules and two other deep reinforcement learning algorithms, namely VDN and standard MAPPO. Our findings demonstrate that enhanced resource flexibility positively impacts scheduling performance, which indicates that enterprises must balance the benefits of flexibility against its implementation costs to satisfy customer demand.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2695241.a: This paper presents a novel machine cognition framework to formulate the axial failure strength of high-strength steel T-joints, addressing the limitations of conventional design models and the scarcity of experimental data. To overcome data scarcity, a hybrid synthetic data generation framework combining bootstrap resampling with feature-specific Gaussian perturbation, bounded by geometric validity conditions of HSS T-joints, and kernel density estimation expands the dataset from 147 to 400 samples. Unlike conventional resampling that relies on exact replication, the proposed approach preserves inter-variable correlations and statistical distributions while ensuring that all generated samples remain within structurally admissible parameter ranges. The framework employs symbolic regression to develop closed-form mathematical expression that achieves exceptional predictive performance, with a coefficient of determination of 0.99. In addition to predictive accuracy, the methodology integrates explainable artificial intelligence to enhance interpretability and explainability, providing physical insights into the influence of geometric, material, and welding parameters. These insights highlight width ratio, brace wall thickness, and weld size as dominant predictors of joint capacity. In contrast to the resource- and time-intensive laboratory tests, the derived expression provides fast, computationally lightweight, and practically scalable tools for capacity estimation in early-stage design. The proposed hybrid framework, therefore, represents a transparent, trustworthy, and efficient artificial intelligence solution for structural analysis and design.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2695245.a: Demand fluctuations, machine downtime, and execution plans’ uncertainties affect production planning and scheduling in flow shops; therefore, these factors must be considered during planning to prevent operational disruptions. Unlike existing static integrated planning and scheduling models or heuristic-based dynamic approaches, this work introduces a closed-loop Digital Twin (DT) framework that preserves the mathematical optimality of a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model while enabling real-time adaptability. Our primary innovation is the systematic and real-time integration of Support Vector Machine (SVM)-based demand forecasting and Association Rule Mining (ARM)-based proactive downtime prediction. We develop a data-driven DT that synchronises the MINLP with live shop-floor data. The framework integrates SVM for demand forecasting and ARM for proactive machine downtime prediction. Through event-driven re-optimisation, the DT continuously updates key parameters and triggers schedule revisions in response to operational deviations. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces total operational costs by 13%, significantly decreases machine waiting times and unscheduled downtime, and improves schedule stability compared to static and data-driven baselines. The results underscore the unique value of closed-loop adaptive systems in enhancing resilience and efficiency. This study bridges the gap between traditional optimisation models and real-world execution to offer more responsive and robust production systems.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2695247.a: With the increasing prevalence of make-to-order production, manufacturing systems are shifting from isolated single-shop to multiple interdependent shops. In the case of lot streaming, downstream assembly is highly sensitive to kitting completeness, inducing strong sublot-level coupling between fabrication and assembly. Existing studies offer limited support for sublot-level fabrication–assembly coordination and seldom exploit feasible time windows for kitting synchronisation. Motivated by metal tube-frame furniture production, this study investigates a sublot-level coordinated fabrication–assembly scheduling problem (SL-FASP) to minimise total tardiness. The system consists of a hybrid flowshop for component fabrication and a flowshop for assembly. Component lots can be split into intermingled sublots, while assembly is performed at the product-sublot level under kitting constraints. A mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model is formulated, and a full active schedule (FAS)-driven solution framework (FAS_SF) is developed. It constructs kitting-consistent schedules by exploiting earliest–latest feasible time windows and improves them through a co-adaptive iterated greedy (CIG)-based improvement phase with FAS-based reverse-encoding and deterministic re-decoding. Results show that FAS_SF achieves the lowest mean ARPI in most real-world-scale and large-scale configurations compared with state-of-the-art heuristics and reduces average total tardiness and runtime by 60.6% and 98.4%, respectively, compared with CPLEX on small-scale instances.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2696434.a: Yard template planning (YTP) is commonly applied at transshipment hubs to reduce transportation costs by assigning storage areas for outbound vessels. With recent advances in digital transformation technologies, terminal operators increasingly rely on simulation-based decision-making to address the uncertain nature of port operations. However, high-fidelity container terminal simulations typically require several minutes to hours per run, and YTP involves a high-dimensional and combinatorial design space. To address these challenges, we propose a domain-informed parallel Bayesian optimisation framework. A Gaussian process (GP) surrogate is presented to efficiently approximate the posterior distribution of terminal performance, thereby enhancing an uncertainty-aware balance between exploration and exploitation. We further integrate a large neighbourhood search (LNS) with the surrogate to navigate the combinatorial design space in parallel. Experimental results show that the proposed approach improves average prediction accuracy by 14.89% and 23.42% over two standard GP surrogates and reduces average vehicle travel time by 4.15%, 1.47%, and 3.27% compared with two Bayesian optimisation approaches and the LNS-based simulation optimisation approach, respectively.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2696436.a: Disassembly of End-of-Life (EOL) products is critical in remanufacturing, as it enables the recovery of valuable components. However, increasing EOL product diversity and uncertainty in product supply and component demand challenge disassembly line design and planning. To address these challenges, we investigate a multi-product reconfigurable disassembly line balancing problem integrated with lot-sizing under uncertainty. A two-stage stochastic programming model is developed to determine line configurations and disassembly plans, aiming to ensure a target profit with high probability. To overcome the stochastic model's reliance on known probability distributions and its sole focus on the likelihood of meeting the target profit, we introduce a novel target-oriented Profit Achievability Index (PAI). The PAI evaluates the achievability of a target profit by jointly considering the average magnitude of profit shortfalls and their tail risk. A new PAI-based distributionally robust optimisation model is then formulated, and an improved bisection search algorithm with a divide-and-conquer strategy is developed to enhance computational efficiency. Experimental results reveal managerial insights into the value of disassembly line reconfigurability and target-oriented modeling. Furthermore, computational experiments on random instances show that the proposed algorithm reduces average solution time by approximately 86% and 72% relative to Gurobi and basic bisection search, respectively.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2696437.a: Local disruptions in Supply Networks (SNs) can propagate, causing impaired connectivity and economic losses. While most research focuses on enhancing SN resilience against such ripple effects, often from a cooperative firm perspective, this study investigates node reinforcement through an overload protection countermeasure with two response parameters. We introduce a Ripple Effect with Protection (REP) model to analyse how SN structure, redundancy, and response parameters affect SN resilience and economic benefit under disruptions. A novel economic metric termed the net benefit is proposed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of these countermeasures. Simulations on synthetic and real-life SNs under random and targeted disruptions reveal that overload protection effectiveness is contingent on SN characteristics and response settings. Notably, while protection generally enhances or maintains resilience, its impact on economic benefit varies: for instance, in SNs with insufficient redundancy, increasing protection level can improve both resilience and net benefit, whereas in sufficiently redundant SNs, net benefit may decline with higher protection levels, indicating an optimal investment threshold. These findings offer managerial insights for balancing SN resilience and economic efficiency.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2696438.a: As emerging contaminant risks intensify, supply chains in pollution-sensitive industries have become increasingly uncertain and vulnerable. Containing pollution risk diffusion and enhancing supply chain resilience therefore constitute urgent theoretical and practical challenges. Based on inter-firm supply and demand relationships, this study constructs a network game model incorporating firm pollution sensitivity, economic exposure, and green investment. By comparing independent firm decision-making, homogeneous decision-making with network effects, and heterogeneous decision-making, this study conducts numerical simulations using data from 391 firms across six typical pollution-sensitive industries. The findings show that complementary business relationships alter the marginal returns to firms’ green investment and may induce free-riding-like strategic dependence under network externalities, thereby weakening preventive green investment incentives and increasing supply-chain network vulnerability. Firms’ green investment decisions are jointly driven by their own pollution sensitivity, potential economic losses, and partners’ risk exposure. Supply-chain topology further moderates the green investment–resilience relationship: when cooperation is limited, higher business concentration strengthens network resilience; when cooperation is intensive but structurally imbalanced, improving the green governance capacity of vulnerable firms and reducing structural asymmetry more effectively curb pollution-risk diffusion. These findings provide implications for stakeholders’ green governance and supply chain risk management decisions.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2696440.a: Effective inventory management requires deciding when to order, how much to order, and how much protection to keep in the form of safety stock and safety lead time. Many recent data-driven approaches still treat lead times, purchasing costs, and defect rates as fixed inputs, and usually optimise replenishment separately from safety buffers. This study proposes a data-driven framework that jointly determines replenishment decisions, safety stock, and safety lead time while accounting for time-varying lead times, purchasing costs, and defect quantities. The approach also uses a custom loss function to reflect the asymmetric consequences of forecast errors in the inventory setting. The method is tested on a real automotive dataset. Results show that it produces inventory decisions that are close to those of an ideal decision-maker and improves cost performance compared with the benchmark approaches considered. Overall, the study shows that integrating forecasting, safety-parameter tuning, and replenishment optimisation can support more effective inventory decisions in dynamic operating environments.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2696443.a: The dynamic flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSSP) presents a challenge for modern flexible manufacturing systems, where heuristic dispatching rules (HDRs) are widely adopted for their rapid response capabilities. While automated design methods such as genetic programming have advanced the field, their reliance on random search operators motivates more structured, knowledge-driven approaches. This paper proposes Evo-TextGrad, a framework combining population-based evolutionary search with large language model (LLM)-driven feedback aggregation. Rather than relying on single-point feedback, Evo-TextGrad collects critique signals across an entire population of candidate HDRs and aggregates them to identify consistent improvement patterns, enhancing rule quality even when local LLMs are used. To enable cost-effective local deployment, a knowledge distillation pipeline automatically constructs a dataset of evolutionary success patterns by capturing prompt-HDR pairs that yield performance improvements. This curated dataset transfers HDR design capability to a local 7B model via LoRA-based fine-tuning, producing ModouGPT. Experiments on 1000 dynamic FJSSP instances against strong load-balancing baselines and evolutionary hyper-heuristic methods show that Evo-TextGrad achieves favourable performance over classical rules and state-of-the-art LLM-based frameworks, while ModouGPT matches larger models at lower resource cost. A real-world flexible manufacturing case study validates industrial effectiveness.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2698797.a: Article title: Automatic demand forecast model selection in supply chains: a forecast value-added analysis of selection strategies, machine learning, and hyperparameter optimisationAuthors: Garred,...

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702047.a: Livestreaming sales (LSS) has become one of the fastest-growing formats in digital commerce, yet rising commission rates render influencer-led livestreaming increasingly costly. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now offer a promising alternative: AI-powered virtual hosts that engage consumers and promote products without commission payments, albeit with lower interactional efficiency. This paper examines the brand's strategic choice between influencer-led and AI-hosted LSS. We develop an analytical model involving a brand and a dual-purpose influencer who values both commission and popularity-related benefits such as follower-base expansion. Our analysis uncovers two opposing mechanisms shaping how cost dynamics affect livestreaming choices. The influencer interactional-compensation effect captures the influencer's tendency to raise interactional richness as product cost increases, thereby helping stabilise demand. In contrast, the AI price-stabilisation effect results in lower interactional investment but more stable pricing. We show that when the influencer cares only about commission earnings, AI hosting is optimal only for low-cost products. If the influencer is profit-popularity driven, however, AI hosting may remain profitable for mid-to-high-cost products when AI is inefficient and popularity incentive is strong. Our results highlight the importance of tailoring livestreaming mode with product cost structure and the moderating role of the influencer's profit-popularity motivation.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702048.a: This paper focuses on an integrated production and truck–drone collaborative delivery problem. The objective is to minimise the makespan. Jobs are first processed on a single machine in the factory and then distributed to their respective customers through a truck–drone pair in a back-and-forth manner. Specifically, the truck transports the processed jobs to the customer area, and at the parking point, the drone with limited flight endurance is launched to complete the final delivery to specific customer locations. Given that drone flight times vary across jobs, the general problem is shown to be strongly NP-hard. We identify two special cases that can be solved in polynomial time: (i) all jobs share the same drone flight time, and (ii) the number of distinct drone flight times is fixed. For both cases, we develop optimal algorithms. For the general case, we propose an approximation algorithm that integrates the First Fit Decreasing algorithm with Johnson's rule. Comprehensive numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702050.a: Buffer zones are essential in production systems to decouple sequential processes. In dense floor storage environments, such as space-constrained brownfield facilities, manual operation is increasingly challenged by severe labor shortages and rising operational costs. Automating these zones requires solving the Buffer Storage, Retrieval, and Reshuffling Problem (BSRRP). While previous work has addressed scenarios where the focus is limited to reshuffling and retrieving a fixed set of items, real-world manufacturing necessitates an adaptive approach that also incorporates arriving unit loads. This paper introduces the Multi-AMR BSRRP, coordinating a robot fleet to manage concurrent reshuffling, alongside time-windowed storage and retrieval tasks, within a shared floor area. We formulate a Binary Integer Programming (IP) model to obtain exact solutions for benchmarking purposes. As the problem is NP-hard, rendering exact methods computationally intractable for industrial scales, we propose a hierarchical heuristic. This approach decomposes the problem into an A* search for task-level sequence planning of unit load placements, and a Constraint Programming (CP) approach for multi-robot coordination and scheduling. Experiments demonstrate orders-of-magnitude computation time reductions compared to the exact formulation. These results confirm the heuristic's viability as responsive control logic for high-density production environments.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702052.a: We study the problem of scheduling engineers who drive to customer sites to perform service tasks. Vehicle speeds and associated CO2 emissions are time-dependent. Customers specify a service time window or choose to participate in a green delivery programme by offering multiple available time windows. This new vehicle routing problem with multiple time windows and time-dependent speeds is formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model to minimise emission costs. The model is then extended to handle scenarios in which customers can offer optional time windows on different days. To solve large instances, we develop a self-adaptive simulated annealing algorithm. For small instances solvable by optimisation software, experimental results show that the algorithm produces near-optimal solutions efficiently. Experiments on instances of different sizes show consistent improvement of the proposed algorithm over the standard simulated annealing. The algorithm is further applied in additional experiments simulating more practical operations. Results demonstrate that incorporating time window flexibility can reduce emission costs and increase the number of customers served under overbooking conditions. Tests under various settings indicate that greater participation in the green delivery programme, or more available time windows per customer, leads to further reductions in emission costs and improved service capacity.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702053.a: This study examines how strategic lean practices (SLPs), including Hoshin Kanri, catchball processes, lean improvement tools, and digital diagnostic capabilities, support the transition toward human-centered, resilient Industry 5.0 manufacturing systems. Drawing on knowledge management theory, strategy deployment literature, and research on Industry 4.0 and 5.0, the study conducts a comparative analysis of four manufacturing cases. The findings suggest that stronger diagnostic infrastructures, including value stream mapping (VSM), dashboards, heat maps, and other digital performance visibility tools, support richer knowledge management processes by enabling more robust combination and internalisation processes within the SECI model. The cases further demonstrate that digitalisation reduces the manual burden associated with data collection and problem identification, enabling organisations to focus more on longitudinal analysis, prioritisation, and continuous improvement. The study also highlights how overly granular target structures can lead to dysfunctional local optimisation, whereas more aggregated strategic deployment mechanisms can strengthen shared ownership across organisational functions. The paper contributes a contingent decision framework for selecting strategic lean practices depending on the strategic challenge, available diagnostic capabilities, and desired Industry 5.0 outcomes.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702054.a: Synchronisation as a logistics concept aims to harmonise material and information flows in production systems and supply chains across different organisations. For instance, in the automotive industry, the Just-in-Sequence concept synchronises suppliers' parts production with manufacturers' assembly, thereby reducing lead times, improving due date reliability, and lowering inventories along the supply chain. Synchronisation has emerged as a key approach to balance logistics performance, cost efficiency, and resilience demands in complex global production networks. In parallel, synchronisation as a physics concept has gained relevance, with applications in architecture, biology, and mechanics. This review article seeks to consolidate these diverse perspectives by examining how synchronisation is conceptualised in logistics and physics. Our aim is to identify potential pathways through which synchronisation mediates both negative and positive effects, thereby contributing to the performance of global production and supply chains. We use a discrete event simulation of a simplified Just-in-Sequence system to illustrate key impact factors of the two synchronisation types. Based on this foundation, we analyze 81 publications from 1986 to 2025 and identify the mathematical foundations of different synchronisation measures and conceptualizations, and describe their linkages to key performance indicators used in industrial practice. The findings provide insights for both scholars and practitioners seeking to better understand the dynamics of complex value systems and to leverage synchronisation as a means of enhancing operational performance.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702056.a: We propose an evaluation framework to enhance U.S. rural hospital efficiency and sustainability amid rising costs and staffing shortages. Moving beyond ‘black-box’ evaluations, we utilise a two-stage Network-Data Envelopment Analysis (N-DEA) Slack-Based Measure model - Resource Allocation and Patient Care Delivery – to analyse internal inefficiencies. To ensure validity, 57 rural hospitals were segmented by size. To capture performance evolution, we integrate the Hicks-Moorsteen Productivity Index to evaluate annual Total Factor Productivity (TFP) shifts. We model hospitals as production systems converting resources into health outcomes. Applied to a 2018–2023 dataset, the model reveals that Patient Care Delivery consistently outperforms Resource Allocation. Longitudinal analysis indicates that while 48 of 57 hospitals recorded net TFP increases, volatility persists, particularly among small and medium facilities. This suggests performance gains are achievable by addressing Resource Allocation bottlenecks. Slack analysis reveals divergent profiles: small hospitals frequently operate with zero slack, whereas the broader sample shows 20% average excess for physicians and certified nurse practitioners. Scenario testing confirms modest reductions (25%) in these roles would enhance efficiency by 1.8%. Conversely, we recommend protecting registered nurse staffing due to minimal slack (6%), as potential efficiency gains are outweighed by patient care risks. This study offers data-driven insights for healthcare decision-makers.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702057.a: The green steel transition requires corporates to operate closed-loop supply chains (CLSCs) that involve operational decisions under heterogeneous data. Although decision models have shifted CLSC operations towards advanced analytics and optimisation, challenges remain in automatically interpreting natural-language requests, enabling data-driven reasoning, and communicating outcomes for actionable decision-making. Motivated by recent progress in large language models (LLMs), we propose an intelligent digital twin-based decision-support method (LMiDTSC) to automatically interpret, reason, and address CLSC operational tasks, and synchronise physical and digital CLSC resources. We develop a knowledge graph, a benchmark, and an accurate query-explanation consistency (AQEC) metric to operate the method and evaluate its effectiveness in supporting decisions on steel distribution and scrap collection. Across focal operational tasks, LMiDTSC outperforms baselines (e.g. GPT-5.2) by 82.73% in AQEC, while its fine-tune outperforms backbones using proprietary models by 93.17% in AQEC. This study advances decision support systems and AI-enabled operations research by integrating LLMs and digital twins for computerised decisions in CLSC operations. This study suggests supply chain practitioners should consider high-performing LLMs for complex operational tasks and exercise caution in scaling in-context learning prompts. Finally, policymakers can accelerate the implementation of such integrated decision support systems by promoting industrial symbiosis and workforce training.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702058.a: This study addresses a gap in the literature by proposing and empirically validating a novel, integrated decision tool for blockchain adoption in supply chains, the Country Level Blockchain Readiness Index for Firms in Supply Chains (CLBRI-FSC). The index integrates five dimensions, including financial support, information technology infrastructure, logistics infrastructure, human capital, and organisational capital. Based on established theoretical frameworks, the index uses secondary data from the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). It employs Min–Max normalisation to standardise indicators and cosine similarity. It calculates readiness scores, offering a replicable and data-driven metric. Results highlight regional differences. Organisations in Northern and Western European countries like Finland, Denmark, Norway, and Belgium show strong readiness in financial and technological infrastructure. Organisations in Southern European countries such as Italy and Portugal exhibit greater readiness in human and organisational capital, reflecting more managerial flexibility and skill development. Organisations in Central and Eastern European countries, including Romania and Bulgaria, show low readiness across most dimensions due to financial, infrastructural, and institutional challenges. The findings provide insights for managers, industry, and policymakers to develop supportive strategies for blockchain adoption.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702059.a: Unreasonable allocation of dock resources can easily cause maintenance task blockage during ship maintenance operations. Moreover, uncertain ship arrival time due to external factors poses significant challenges for maintenance scheduling. Therefore, this work investigates a multi-ship co-dock maintenance scheduling problem with limited dock capacity and uncertain ship arrival time. To solve this problem efficiently, this work first employs chance-constrained programming to address uncertain ship arrival time. It is then integrated with a constraint programming (CP) model to generate a robust multi-ship co-dock maintenance schedule. Meanwhile, a PPO-driven matheuristic algorithm is further developed to improve the solution efficiency for larger instances. The PPO-driven matheuristic integrates proximal policy optimisation (PPO) and the CP decomposition model. PPO adaptively adjusts the search behaviour. Meanwhile, the CP decomposition model performs local refinements to further improve promising solutions. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed CP model and the PPO-driven matheuristic. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the CP model. Compared with the mixed-integer programming model, it delivers significantly better solving performance. The key components of the PPO-driven matheuristic algorithm contribute positively to algorithmic performance, and the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art metaheuristic algorithms.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702564.a: This paper dvelops a mathematical model for designing a multi-echelon Bone China Supply Chain (BCSC), aiming to minimise total costs minus revenues through decisions related to facility location, supplier selection, and material flow quantities across the network. The model explicitly incorporates simultaneous uncertainty in both raw material supply and product demand, which is addressed using a Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) approach. Additionally, part of the required raw material is obtained through voluntarily contributed recycled sources. To solve the proposed model, we employ the L-shaped Benders decomposition algorithm and an enhanced version that incorporates a warm-up strategy to improve computational efficiency. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves higher profitability and better demand fulfillment rates under various uncertainty scenarios compared to traditional stochastic optimisation methods. Moreover, the inclusion of voluntary recycled inputs significantly reduces operational costs and enhances the overall economic performance of the BCSC. The results also confirm the effectiveness of the warm-up strategy in accelerating convergence and improving solution quality, particularly in large-scale instances.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2702566.a: In today's turbulent business environment, the significance of supply chain resilience (SCRES) has surged. Although SCRES capabilities and their potential impact on performance have been extensively explored, supply chain management (SCM) remains human-centric and depends heavily on individuals and teams making effective decisions. However, the extant literature on individual- and team-level capabilities required to enhance SCRES remains fragmented. This study addresses this gap through a systematic literature review (SLR) of extant knowledge in this area. We develop an integrative framework of Dynamic Human-related Capabilities for resilience by extending the Dynamic Managerial Capability (DMC) theory to examine how individuals and teams enhance SCRES. Although relevant, DMC theory mainly emphasises managers’ roles within organisations. To provide a more comprehensive understanding of human related capabilities for enhanced SCRES, we extend the analysis to employees and teams, within and across organisations. We examine research inquiries and analytical models from 77 studies, focusing on three dynamic human-related capabilities: (i) social capital, (ii) human capital, and (iii) cognition. We identify key practices associated with each capability and explain their roles in enhancing SCRES. Furthermore, we propose a future research agenda that puts human-centric factors at the core of SCRES.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2703283.a: In modern industry, proactive maintenance is crucial for preventing failures and reducing costs. However, most existing data-driven prognostic frameworks remain limited in their ability to support realistic maintenance decisions, primarily due to a persistent disconnect between predictive modelling and maintenance modelling. While deep learning methods have advanced life prediction accuracy, they often neglect the pervasive reality of imperfect maintenance (IM), where maintenance actions only partially restore equipment health. This disconnect is compounded when IM modelling, traditionally grounded in reliability statistics, is not adapted to leverage real-time, data-driven predictions and their associated uncertainties. To bridge this gap, this study proposes an innovative integrated framework that closes the loop between uncertainty-aware prediction and maintenance optimisation. Our core contribution is a systematic methodology that includes: a novel Weighted Interval Fusion (WIF) method for high-confidence remaining useful life (RUL) prediction; a hybrid degradation model that uses Bayesian inference to dynamically select the most suitable IM model; and a dynamic maintenance strategy guided by a risk perception function, which explicitly couples prediction uncertainty with failure urgency. Extensive experiments show that our framework not only improves prediction accuracy but also yields more cost-effective and reliable maintenance strategies, thereby providing a prescriptive foundation for intelligent maintenance.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2703757.a: The convergence of Industry 5.0 imperatives, sustainability challenges, and compulsory reporting standards necessitate advances in manufacturing analysis. Digital Twins (DTs) enable real-time manufacturing monitoring and optimization, yet remain disconnected from corporate sustainability reporting (SR). This separation restricts leveraging operational data for mandatory disclosures and seeking operational improvements from sustainability reporting insights. DT research has predominantly focused on energy efficiency, with limited attention to broader environmental dimensions. We address this gap by developing a System-of-Systems framework integrating operational DTs with SR requirements. The gap, identified through literature analysis, is confirmed using expert interviews. We identify data mismatches between DT systems with process-level data and SR using periodic, facility-level data. Applying System-of-Systems theory, we develop a four-step framework (Mapping, Matching, Measuring, Modeling) enabling systematic translation between two independent systems. The framework demonstrates how manufacturing systems DTs can both supply and respond to SR outputs. Interview cited examples using a simplified manufacturing system and exemplified SR standard demonstrate applicability. The outcome is a structured approach for integrating DTs to support SR generation, and for SR insights to inform DT-enabled operational scenarios for performance enhancement. The contribution of the DT and SR framework is both to modeling advancement as well as management practice.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2703758.a: Process planning bridges product design and manufacturing and increasingly involves multiple types of flexibility. As an NP-hard combinatorial optimisation problem, it poses substantial methodological challenges, yet effective optimisation is critical for improving production performance. This paper presents a review of process planning from an operations research perspective, covering models, algorithms, and benchmarks. We systematically classify mathematical programming models according to key characteristics, including model class, flexibility types, and objective settings, and highlight recent advances in linearisation techniques and compact formulations. From an algorithmic standpoint, we review and categorise solution paradigms, encompassing metaheuristics, multi-objective optimisation, deterministic methods, heuristics, and reinforcement learning, and analyse their respective strengths and limitations. In addition, we compile benchmark test cases together with technical specifications and best-known solutions to support systematic performance comparison. Finally, we identify research gaps and outline promising future directions, with particular emphasis on advanced optimisation methods and practically relevant modelling.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2703764.a: Assembly lines are widely used for mass production. Their design and operation of such systems involve the resolution of multiple problems, among which the assembly line balancing problem (ALBP) is one of the most studied. An ALBP typically involves at least two interrelated decisions aimed at optimising line efficiency: (1) determining the sequence in which operations must be performed within the assembly line and (2) assigning these tasks to the stations that constitute the assembly line. This study presents a general methodology for solving a broad range of ALBPs based on the observation that many such problems can be decomposed into interrelated subproblems. The proposed method leverages the fact that once a task sequence is fixed, optimal station assignments can be obtained through a dynamic programming (DP) recursion. To illustrate the proposed methodology, we derive DP formulations for multiple ALBP variants and integrate them into heuristic frameworks that explore a solution space represented by task sequences. Computational experiments using a genetic algorithm and a local search procedure demonstrate the adaptability and effectiveness of the proposed approach. In particular, for sequence-dependent and chance-constrained assembly line balancing problems, the method achieves higher-quality solutions in shorter computational times than current state-of-the-art techniques.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2704025.a: Modern manufacturing faces growing challenges from market volatility, resource uncertainty, and the need for quick adaptation. Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems (RMSs) offer a flexible adaptable solution; however, scheduling becomes more complex when worker availability is uncertain. Workers in RMSs represent limited and mobile resources, whose uncertain availability can severely disrupt production efficiency. This paper investigates the non-identical parallel machine scheduling problem in an RMS under stochastic worker availability. To tackle this complex optimisation problem, a two-stage stochastic programming model is developed. In the first stage, job-to-machine assignments are determined as here-and-now decisions. The second stage involves optimising job sequencing, machine configurations, and worker assignments after the worker availability scenarios are revealed. To solve this problem, a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and an L-shaped Decomposition (LD) method are developed to minimise the expected makespan. To enhance solution efficiency, a novel CP-LD is proposed, where the master problem uses MILP while subproblems employ Constraint Programming (CP). Computational results show that the proposed CP-LD method outperforms the MILP and LD methods in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. The sensitivity analysis provides insights into the impact of various system parameters on the expected makespan performance, highlighting the critical importance of workforce management.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2704027.a: Relief resource allocation is a pivotal component of humanitarian aid during disaster response. The urgency of our work stems from two temporal constraints: time-sensitive medical intervention (golden hour therapeutic window) to prevent infected patient deterioration, and demand dynamics with hourly/daily increments in affected areas. The humanitarian supply chain relies on a dual reserve system (physical stockpiles and production capacity) to meet these demands. We address the interdependency between demand volatility and emergency response activation by developing a prescriptive optimisation framework for relief resource allocation under time restrictions. The framework partitions relief resource pooling stations endogenously into virtual units for modelling and proposes a three-phase solution: baseline (no time restrictions), feasible (with time restrictions) and optimal (with time restrictions) allocation. This method corrects discrepancies between planned and actual resource needs, critical in pandemic scenarios where delays heighten mortality risks and resource misallocation. Simulations on bioterrorism-induced disease outbreaks validate the framework. Results show: (1) optimised resource allocation while maintaining differential time restrictions at each affected area, (2) enhanced dual reserve system performance, operational robustness and resilience and (3) time restrictions directly shape allocation schemes by leveraging available reserves. The framework applies to scenarios like the COVID-19 pandemic, offering actionable managerial insights.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2704028.a: In CNC cutting scenarios such as large-scale shipbuilding, net-like scrap skeletons formed by cutting often lead to difficulties in separating nested parts, and their dimensions frequently exceed the handling limits of automated equipment or scrap containers, thus necessitating further segmentation. Existing ‘skeleton cut line’ (SCL) processes heavily rely on manual experience, making it difficult to balance scrap disposal requirements and processing efficiency. To address this, we propose the Joint Optimisation Problem of Skeleton Cut Line Layout and Cutting Path Planning, aiming to synergistically determine the SCL layout, cutting sequence, and entry points to minimise total processing costs under process constraints. We construct a mixed-integer linear programming model that integrates the Extended Precedence-Constrained Generalised Travelling Salesman Problem with the Weighted Set Covering Problem, and propose a two-stage heuristic hybrid solution approach of ‘geometry generation–dynamic optimisation’. The first stage constructs a finite high-quality candidate SCL set via geometric rules; the second employs a hybrid heuristic integrating Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search, Simulated Annealing, and Local Search for efficient joint dynamic optimisation. Experiments on standard benchmarks and real-world industrial instances verify the model accuracy and demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in solution quality, efficiency, and robustness, confirming its practical applicability.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2704029.a: In recent years, geopolitical events such as Brexit and the U.S.–China trade war have become increasingly frequent and have had significant impacts on supply chains. Supply chain reconfiguration has been recognised as an effective approach to addressing geopolitical risks (GPRs). However, existing literature reviews in this field exhibit several limitations that motivate us to advance the understanding of supply chain reconfiguration amid GPRs. Accordingly, we conduct a systematic literature review of 92 high-quality journal articles published between 2015 and May 2026 to identify key emerging topics, their antecedents–decisions–outcomes (ADO) frameworks, and the associated research gaps and future research directions. Specifically, we apply a topic modelling technique combined with a semantic validation approach to classify the articles into five topics and rank their scores of emergence. This process identifies three emerging topics: supply chain reconfigurations in advanced technology sectors, adaptive risk management approaches, and diversification strategies. For each emerging topic, we develop topic-specific research frameworks using an ADO framework incorporating moderators. Based on identified gaps, we propose tailored future research directions for each emerging topic. Overall, this study advances the understanding of supply chain reconfiguration amid GPRs and provides actionable insights for future researchers and practitioners.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2704030.a: Disassembly scheduling for End-of-Life (EOL) products, particularly EV batteries, exhibits dynamic structural uncertainty and physical degradation characteristics. However, existing scheduling models are predominantly static and fail to fully capture the distinctive stochastic features and operation skipping patterns of such disassembly systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the process as a Markov Decision Process and propose a Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (H-MADRL) framework. To enhance practical applicability, a Hierarchical State Embedding module acts as a digital perception layer to quantify physical risks. Meanwhile, a Physics-Informed Dual-Agent mechanism coordinates task-machine assignments, and a Constraint-Compliant Masking layer ensures strict adherence to Standard Operating Procedures. Averaged over multiple independent runs, the framework achieves a 45.6% increase in profit rate and a 16.9% reduction in makespan compared to standard reinforcement learning and heuristic baselines. Ultimately, this approach secures shop-floor adaptability and significantly advances managerial precision in balancing economic density with operational throughput under stochastic constraints.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2705302.a: Steelmaking–continuous casting (SCC) production scheduling is a critical step for optimising charge combinations, enhancing process compactness, and reducing energy consumption, thereby influencing the production efficiency and economic benefits of steel enterprises. However, the small batch sizes and extensive product variety inherent in modern steelmaking substantially increase scheduling complexity, making it difficult to rapidly generate feasible production plans. Therefore, we incorporate deep learning (DL) into the surrogate Lagrangian relaxation (SLR) framework to accelerate the acquisition of scheduling schemes by replacing the costly process of accurately solving subproblems with predicting ‘good-enough’ subproblem solutions. First, we propose a novel pointer network (GDPN) that integrates gated recurrent unit (GRU) with dot-product attention (DPA) to predict subproblem solutions in the Lagrange decomposition-coordination process. Subsequently, a dual-phase masking (DM) mechanism is developed during both the training and inference of GDPN to enforce the feasibility of the surrogate subproblem constraints caused by the continuous casting process in SCC. Finally, extensive numerical experiments and an industrial study with different scales demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DM-GDPN-SLR method.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2705306.a: We analyse a supply chain with a manufacturer and an influencer selling products by live streaming. The influencer can introduce self-operated products and choose between competitive pricing strategy (Scenario CM) and sequential pricing strategy (Scenario SQ). The content switching level and influencer power impact the demand, which are crucial factors influencing decisions. Additionally, we consider the long-term effect, where live streaming slices or product recommendation logos continue to drive sales after live streaming. We find that in Scenario CM, the manufacturer's optimal production quantity initially declines and then rises as the long-term effect, while in Scenario SQ, it consistently increases. The influencer's optimal profit initially declines and then rises as the long-term effect in both scenarios. When the influencer adopts Scenario SQ, introducing self-operated products always benefits her. However, in Scenario CM, the decision depends on the long-term effect. The manufacturer's and influencer's preferred pricing strategies vary based on the long-term effect. If the long-term effect is high (low), Scenario SQ is preferred to avoid direct competition, while if moderate, Scenario CM is preferred. This paper is the first examining pricing strategies for influencer-operated products, offering valuable insights on when to incorporate self-operated products into the live streaming.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2705317.a: Cloud manufacturing facilitates collaborative production by integrating distributed manufacturing resources via service-oriented platforms. However, its scheduling process is constrained by resource heterogeneity, complex task dependencies, and inefficient platform-enterprise coordination. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach for multi-task scheduling that integrates a contract net protocol (CNP) with graph neural networks (GNNs). First, a platform-enterprise collaborative scheduling framework is proposed. Then, two CNP-based schemes are designed and extended into a Dynamic CNP (DCNP) which updates evaluation weights to improved service selection. Moreover, an RGCN-LDDQN algorithm is proposed, which integrates relational graph convolutional networks (RGCN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and double deep Q-network (DDQN) to model inter-task dependencies and support global scheduling decisions. A bi-level priority constraint is integrated to mitigate conflicts, and a priority-aware P-RGCN-LDDQN is obtained, which enhances feasibility and stability. Subtasks are autonomously scheduled using a genetic algorithm at the enterprise layer based on platform-issued objectives and constraints. Simulations with respect to automotive parts assembly tasks are conducted. Results indicate that, under DCNP, RGCN-LDDQN reduces makespan by 21.88% and comprehensive cost by 15.64% compared to conventional DDQN, while maintaining service quality. Additionally, P-RGCN-LDDQN achieves further reductions of 9.15% and 6.69% over RGCN-LDDQN.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2706627.a: Allocating limited resources (like medicines, professional cares, or hospital beds) across multiple treatments for diverse patients is challenging, especially when choices must be made under uncertainty using grouped data from published clinical studies, such as Sample Average Treatment Effects (SATEs) and Conditional Average Treatment Effects (CATEs). Existing frameworks are often limited to single-intervention settings and do not exploit the value of granular subgroup data. This paper bridges that gap by adapting robust allocation to the summary-evidence regime in which a multi-intervention planner must work with marginally stratified SATE/CATE summaries. Specifically, we propose a tractable approach that maximises the worst-case aggregate patient benefit under a budget constraint. We formulate a hierarchy of models, from a baseline SATE-informed model to an advanced CATE-informed model, and further extend it to capture pre-specified second-order interaction effects. They can be solved through mixed-integer linear programming. Using a case study of COPD vaccination grounded in clinical and population data, our numerical experiments show that allocations based on stratified CATEs achieve substantially higher performance than those based on aggregate SATEs or a stylised risk-based heuristic. The results highlight the significant benefit of systematically incorporating detailed clinical evidence to create more effective and reliable healthcare allocation strategies.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2706628.a: The utilisation of variable sublots in scheduling increases machine efficiency through operation overlap, yet its performance is vulnerable to processing time uncertainty, which can propagate delays and erode robustness. This paper tackles the flexible job shop scheduling problem with variable sublots (FJSP-VS) under such uncertainty, seeking to harness lot streaming efficiency while rigorously managing downside risk. We propose a risk-aware, integrated framework coupling multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for adaptive coordination with a scenario-based, conditional value-at-risk(CVaR)-enhanced mixed-integer program (MILP) for robust sublot planning. The MARL component handles dynamic, operation-level scheduling across flexible routes, while the CVaR-enhanced MILP provides a formal hedge against severe makespan outcomes in sublot partitioning, machine assignment, and timing decisions. Computational results on established benchmarks reveal that the proposed framework consistently surpasses risk-neutral and alternative robust schedulers. The method reduces the CVaR0.9 of makespan by up to about 2% while maintaining competitive average makespan performance, resulting in more stable scheduling outcomes under processing-time uncertainty.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2707319.a: Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) has evolved from a long-standing quality philosophy into a comprehensive, data-driven, and sustainability-oriented paradigm for modern industry. This editorial introduces the Special Issue on ZDM, which comprises twelve papers that collectively advance the scientific, technological, and managerial foundations for achieving defect-free production in digitally connected manufacturing environments. The issue builds upon the ZDM life-cycle framework, which integrates core strategies within a continuous loop of data collection, analysis, decision-making, and adaptive learning. The collected contributions address key enabling domains, including data analytics, artificial intelligence, explainable AI, digital assets, cost modelling, human–AI collaboration, human-centric implementation, machine-vision maturity assessment, and the integration of Lean, Industry 4.0, and Industry 5.0 principles. Collectively, they demonstrate the growing maturity of ZDM as both a research field and an industrial practice. Emerging directions highlight sustainability and circularity, standardisation through interoperable data architectures such as AAS and GAIA-X, and human-centric readiness for implementation. The future outlook identifies six research priorities, semantic interoperability, hybrid intelligence, lifecycle integration, standardised benchmarks, cybersecurity, and human-centric design, positioning ZDM as a cornerstone for resilient, intelligent, and sustainable manufacturing.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2707320.a: This article investigates an integrated production and distribution scheduling problem considering order acceptance (OA-IPDS) with committed delivery dates. It integrates order acceptance, distributed heterogeneous factories, inventory, and a hub-spoke delivery network within a complex system for producing customised orders, aiming to minimize total operating costs, including rejection, production, transportation, inventory, and overdue costs. Accepted orders are split into jobs and then enter the production system. Completed jobs are transported from factories to service centers, and then orders with all their jobs arrive and are delivered from service centers to customers. A mixed integer programming model is formulated and further enhanced by a proposed dominance rule, for which a logic-based Benders decomposition (LBBD) method and a branch-and-check search framework are also developed. The proposed LBBD method divides the problem into the master problem of order acceptance and job assignment and the subproblem of production and distribution scheduling. A hybrid algorithm, TS_LBBD, integrating tabu search and the LBBD method, is also proposed to further enhance computational performance. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can generate optimal or near-optimal solutions efficiently and validate the OA-IPDS model, analyze the sensitivity of key cost factors, and provide valuable managerial insights for practitioners.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2708152.a: This paper investigates a complex scheduling problem originating from real-world pharmaceutical workshops, characterised by the coexistence of reentrant and skippable operations, which we define as the hybrid flowshop scheduling problem with reentrant and skippable operations (HFSP_RAS). The core challenge lies in effectively handling cross-stage operational dependencies, along with strict machine cleaning and transfer time constraints. To accurately capture these complex industrial constraints and to provide highly effective exact benchmarks, two mathematical models are developed: a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and a Constraint Programming (CP) model. Considering the demand for real-time computational efficiency in modern manufacturing, we further develop a heuristic approach that integrates a Construction Scheme (CS) and Critical Path Search (CPS), named CS-CPS. Specifically, the CS adopts a dual-job encoding and a two-phase active decoding mechanism to generate high-quality initial schedules. The CPS further improves the solutions by introducing a critical-path-based search and a neighbourhood pruning strategy. This paper compares the CS-CPS with the MILP and CP models, constructive heuristics, and metaheuristics. The results demonstrate that the proposed CS-CPS, while bridging the computational gap of exact solvers, consistently outperforms the compared algorithms in terms of solution quality and stability. Finally, validation based on real-world production data further confirms its superiority.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2708614.a: Article title: Strategic lean practices for Industry 5.0 manufacturingAuthor: Søberg, Peder Veng, Rasmus Sorth and Samuel Brüning LarsenJournal: International Journal of Production ResearchDOI: htt...

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709043.a: Live streaming is increasingly being applied in the agricultural industry by directly connecting farmers with consumers and shifting supply chains from wholesale contracts to revenue-sharing contracts. This transformation grants farmers greater authority over product selection, including decisions regarding cosmetic standards for produce. Motivated by this practice, this study explores cosmetic standard authority and its supply chain implications within an agricultural live-streaming context involving a farmer and a live streamer. We find that under either authority model, when consumer additional utility for high-standard produce is high, the decision maker prefers selling high-standard produce and otherwise opts for low-standard produce. Surprisingly, a higher agency fee rate makes both parties more likely to sell low-standard produce. When consumer additional utility for high-standard produce is either very high or very low, consensus on unified cosmetic standards can be reached; otherwise, their preferences diverge. In such conflicting cases, live streamer-controlled standards lead to greater farmer effort but also to higher food loss and lower consumer welfare. Interestingly, under certain conditions, either party controlling the decision right can improve overall supply chain profit. This study highlights live-streaming's role in transforming agricultural supply chains and offers managerial insights into cosmetic standard authority and food loss.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709045.a: Manual operations remain a significant part of modern manufacturing, maintaining the role of Methods-Time Measurement (MTM) as a framework for improving productivity and standardising work processes. Despite its usefulness, conducting MTM analysis is a labour intensive task requiring specialised expertise. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) provide a promising path for streamlining MTM analysis. This study establishes a performance baseline for LLMs in this domain by assessing their capabilities when provided with meticulously detailed work descriptions and a comprehensive MTM knowledge base. To this end, we evaluated the analyses generated by DeepSeek-V3.2-reasoner, GPT-5.2-pro, Gemini-2.5-pro, and Qwen3-14B by comparing them against expert-validated ground truths across eleven working scenarios. Our findings suggest that LLMs can accurately perform MTM analysis when supplied with detailed work descriptions and domain knowledge. GPT-5.2-pro and Gemini-2.5-pro proved especially capable, perfectly analysing five and six scenarios, respectively, across ten experimental runs. Despite this success, challenges remain when tasks involve subtle rule applications or steps that are implied rather than stated. Although LLMs significantly reduce analysis time and effort, expert validation remains critical for reliable deployment. These results demonstrate the viability of LLMs as assistive tools for MTM practitioners.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709049.a: The human–robot collaborative assembly line balancing problem (HRC-ALBP), which incorporates collaborative robots (cobots), has recently garnered considerable attention for its potential to enhance productivity and support efficient, human-centered working environments. However, the natural variability in human task times introduces uncertainty, creating challenges for task assignment in collaborative settings. To address this issue, this study proposes a robust local search genetic–particle swarm optimisation (RGP) algorithm for solving the robust HRC-ALBP under task time uncertainty. The proposed algorithm generates line configurations while mitigating excessive solution conservativeness. Numerical experiments were conducted under task time variability to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The results verify that the algorithm produces more stable line configurations. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses were performed by varying both the number of cobots and the coefficient of variation of task times. Consequently, assembly lines designed using the RGP algorithm exhibit substantially higher reliability in sustaining uninterrupted production flow. Moreover, these analyses examine the operator assignment strategies required to establish a stable assembly line, depending on the number of cobots and the coefficient of variation of task times. The results indicate that stable assembly line design critically depends on appropriate operator assignment strategies.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709051.a: We study a material requirement planning (MRP) problem for customised assemble-to-order (ATO) systems in which order-specific bills of materials (BOMs) are unknown when orders are placed and are determined during design lead times, while component replenishment lead times are stochastic. MRP for general ATO systems has long been considered analytically intractable; the combination of uncertain BOMs, delayed BOM revelation, and stochastic replenishment lead times in a dynamic customisation environment further enlarges the state space and strengthens the coupling between replenishment and allocation. We propose a structure-aware deep reinforcement learning framework. Our approach utilises a graph-based encoder and a GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) module to effectively extract features from the product-component requirements and stochastic pipeline dynamics. Leveraging these features, we employ a dual-policy head that simultaneously outputs state-dependent parameters for base-stock replenishment and allocation strategies, thereby preserving the interpretability of classical inventory rules. We further introduce structure-based regularisation terms, inspired by structural patterns suggested by simplified ATO systems, to encourage economically meaningful behaviour and improve robustness. Numerical experiments show lower cost and competitive on-time fulfillment in the base case and in stress regimes with high BOM uncertainty, long replenishment lead times, tight delivery windows, and high backlog penalties.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709052.a: Live-streaming commerce has emerged as a significant and powerful sales force. This new type of commerce enables consumers to engage in real-time interactions while making purchases over the Internet. An increasing number of companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, have adopted live-streaming commerce to attract and engage consumers. Our study investigates the supplier's optimal strategy in response to the fast-growing live-streaming commerce and explores the most effective way to collaborate with third-party livestreamers. We first analyze the impacts of inter-channel cannibalisation upon introducing the new live-streaming channel and find that suppliers should stay with the traditional online channel unless the live-streaming channel can increase the market size significantly. We then assess suppliers' choice in live-streaming mode: self-streaming versus collaborating with professional livestreamers. Our results suggest that collaboration is more profitable only if the third-party livestreamers have a substantial edge in influence level compared to self-streaming. Our analysis also explains the scenario in which suppliers initially choose to sell products through the third-party live-streaming channel but later decide to switch back to self-streaming.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709053.a: Behavioural newsvendor research has documented persistent deviations from optimal ordering – demand chasing, pull-to-center, and anchoring – yet the psychological foundations underlying these biases remain underspecified. We distinguish two constructs: cognitive reflection (CRT), the disposition to override intuitive responses, and math self-efficacy (MSE), a domain-specific motivational belief supporting the persistent application of rule-based reasoning under uncertainty. Using a repeated-round laboratory newsvendor experiment (N = 43 participants, 100 incentivized rounds), we examine the associations between CRT, MSE, and profit, whether MSE attenuates demand-chasing bias, and whether MSE moderates round-by-round learning. CRT and MSE are positively associated with profit, and the estimates are consistent with an indirect association linking CRT to performance via MSE. MSE significantly attenuates demand-chasing bias, primarily in later rounds as participants gain task experience. By contrast, MSE does not moderate the rate of learning but is associated with greater within-subject stability and consistency of ordering behaviour, consistent with motivational stability rather than cognitive bias correction. These findings indicate that reasoning style and motivational beliefs play complementary roles in reducing decision biases: CRT supports analytic override of intuitive responses, whereas MSE sustains consistent rule-based ordering under uncertainty. The study advances the psychological foundations of behavioural operations and informs training and decision-support systems.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2709145.a: The shift to shorter product life cycles and higher customisation demands has made manufacturing flexibility essential. However, the traditional robotic cell production method, equipped with either stationary robotic arms or robotic arms moving along railways, lacks the scalability and reconfigurability to meet volatile demand. Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) provide a promising alternative. Thus, in this study, to enhance production flexibility and efficiency, we introduce a new feature to the traditional robotic cell scheduling method by introducing shared robotic arms facilitated by AMRs. Specifically, AMRs can serve a set of machines across cells; operations in each job are allowed to be processed in different robotic cells concurrently. Additionally, we propose a simulated annealing-based matheuristic algorithm. In this approach, the mathematical programming technique is embedded into the simulated annealing algorithm to determine the optimal heterogeneous AMR routing (HAR). Computational experiments validate the proposed manufacturing method and reveal its suitability in two scenarios: deployment in a compact production configuration and the processing of heterogeneous jobs with bottleneck operations. The effectiveness of the proposed method primarily stems from its capacity to boost machine utilisation, leading to a considerable decrease in makespan.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2711058.a: This paper addresses a dual-resource constrained flexible job-shop scheduling problem (DRC-FJSSP) motivated by operational challenges in a French textile sewing workshop. Given the significant labour costs associated with Made-in-France garment production and the high variability of incoming orders, the scheduling objective is to maximise operator productivity over a short planning horizon. The problem is modelled using two frameworks: Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) and Constraint Programming (CP). A constructive heuristic is presented, the Lowest Continuity Score (LCS) heuristic, is introduced to efficiently maximise operator throughput at industrial scale. A benchmark of industrial instances is derived from real production data. Computational experiments show that exact methods cannot solve instances beyond 200 operations within one hour, while the LCS heuristic consistently achieves solutions within 23% of the analytical upper bound across the large majority of instance classes and quartiles, with gaps below 20% for medium and large instances (Q2–Q4). A second heuristic, the Earliest Starting Time Interval (ESTI), is proposed to improve the balance between productivity and due-date satisfaction. The results indicate that, relative to LCS, ESTI significantly decreases total tardiness while maintaining productivity at a comparable level. This makes it a useful option for practitioners facing urgent orders.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2711893.a: Achieving net-zero manufacturing requires robust strategies that balance environmental, economic, and operational priorities while aligning with global sustainability targets. Integrating advanced decision-making methodologies with comprehensive sustainability frameworks is crucial for guiding climate-neutral industrial transformation. This study develops a modular decision-aid model, namely the Net-Zero Manufacturing Location Decision-Aid Model, for evaluating net-zero manufacturing facility locations from a production-system and logistics-readiness perspective. The model systematically incorporates ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) and HSE (Health, Safety, Environment) criteria and operationalises them through Picture Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (PiF-SWARA) and Picture Fuzzy Additive Ratio Assessment (PiF-ARAS). Expert judgments are aggregated through picture fuzzy logic, capturing uncertainty and subjectivity inherent in real-world decision environments. Results demonstrate that environmental and safety dimensions are the most influential factors in site selection for net-zero manufacturing, while governance and health play a moderate role, and social criteria are relatively less impactful. Sensitivity analysis confirms the stability and robustness of the model across various weighting scenarios. The proposed framework provides actionable insights for decision-makers and policymakers aiming to enable climate-neutral manufacturing investments. This study contributes a scalable, transparent, and replicable methodology, supporting the strategic alignment of industrial development with circular economy principles and smart production technologies.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2711894.a: The semiconductor industry supply chain is complex, with globally distributed production processes and tightly interconnected segments. By controlling the production and supply of essential technologies and equipment, ‘bottleneck’ firms often dominate specific segments of the supply chain, making them critical to the manufacturing processes of advanced semiconductors. For instance, they dictate specific processes or product types, invest in innovative technologies, and protect their intellectual property to establish new markets with high entry barriers. Additionally, we find bottleneck firms who have support from their governments to maintain a competitive edge over rivals. Through social network analysis, we identify that there are eight bottleneck firms of high nodal centrality. We then present case study results of these firms on their local ego networks, how they have created strategic bottlenecks and detail government actions/interventions in preserving or challenging their bottlenecks. A Kraljic perspective is used to classify these eight firms into leverage, strategic, non-critical and bottleneck partners. Furthermore, we aim to make a theoretical contribution to the bodies of production research knowledge on supply – chain bottlenecks and structural power.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2711895.a: Green hydrogen (GH) and green ammonia (GA) are promising solutions for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors and enabling large-scale renewable energy storage and transportation. As interest in GH increases, optimising production facilities facing intermittent renewable energy supply is essential for economic viability. Existing studies often oversimplify uncertainty in scenario probabilities for renewable generation and ignore interactions with electricity markets. To address this gap, this study develops a stochastic optimisation framework for designing grid-connected GH–GA systems and extends it to a distributionally robust optimisation formulation to hedge against ambiguity in those scenario probabilities. Market participation is captured through a pay-as-cleared electricity market mechanism. A hyperparameter calibration for scenario count and divergence budget validated through out-of-sample testing shows improved reliability compared to conventional stochastic methods. A case study on Canada's Eastern coast identifies a hybrid wind-solar system with grid backup a cost-effective configuration, achieving hydrogen and ammonia costs of $4.17/kg and $0.72/kg, respectively. Sensitivity analyses show that rising electricity prices favour increased on-site wind capacity and reduced grid reliance. Results highlight that optimal system design and market strategies are region-specific, project economics remain stable across wide ranges of market pricing and grid accessibility, and accounting for uncertainty improves economic performance and production stability.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2711897.a: Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are increasingly deployed in automated warehouses, robotic fulfilment centres, and smart logistics environments, where agents must coordinate under communication, energy, and operational constraints. Inefficient communication policies can increase energy consumption, create bottlenecks, and overload specific agents, reducing long-term system robustness. This paper proposes a multi-period coordination and communication scheduling framework for industrial MAS formulated as a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model. The framework jointly optimises coordination efficiency, communication-energy consumption, and workload balance (Fairness) while considering finite coordination capacities, bounded communication durations, dynamic communication conditions, and coordination-communication dependencies. Two multi-objective solution approaches are developed: a desirability-based reformulation to identify balanced compromise solutions and an ε-constraint formulation to analyze Pareto trade-offs among efficiency, energy use, and fairness. Industrial-scale benchmark instances inspired by autonomous warehouse operations are generated to evaluate the framework under heterogeneous capacities, workload variability, sparse communication topologies, and dynamic energy conditions. Computational experiments and sensitivity analyses show that communication energy is a major operational bottleneck. Results reveal scarcity and saturation regimes in which moderate increases in communication-energy availability significantly improve coordination performance, whereas further resource relaxation yields diminishing returns. The framework provides a tractable and interpretable tool for robust coordination and communication management in large-scale industrial MAS.

10.1080/00207543.2026.2718797.a: The reliable operation of heavy construction equipment is critical for project productivity; however, spare parts inventory decisions for such equipment are often made using intuition-based or oversimplified approaches, leading to unnecessary costs and equipment downtime. In particular, construction-specific spare parts management lacks systematic, data-driven frameworks that account for uncertainty, multiple decision criteria, and operational criticality. To address this gap, this study proposes a hybrid decision-support framework that integrates Fuzzy Combinative Distance-Based Assessment (Fuzzy CODAS) with Always Better Control (ABC) analysis to optimise spare parts inventory for hydraulic excavators.
